weeks.title: Six weeks out: the three jobs that matter
weeks.headline: You do not have to be ready for everything, only for the first week. Start with the car seat.

expect.feeds: Not yet. From day one, 8 to 12 feeds in 24 hours
expect.sleep: Yours matters now. Bank early nights while you can
expect.newThisWeek: Baby is practising sucking and swallowing in there

focuses: Book the car seat fitting, or install it and get it checked
Do the hospital tour and find out where to park at 2am
Start the leave paperwork: employer, Centrelink, Medicare
weeks.heads_up: Cot setup and the Red Nose rules come next week. Buy nothing until you have read them.

weeks.title: Set the cot up to Red Nose rules
weeks.headline: A safe sleep space is the one thing you cannot improvise at 3am, so build it now.

expect.feeds: Not yet. Decide now who does which night feeds
expect.sleep: Newborns sleep 14 to 17 hours a day, never all at once
expect.nappies: Stock up. Newborns go through 8 to 12 nappies a day
expect.newThisWeek: Baby can hear both your voices clearly now, so talk away

focuses: Firm flat mattress, no pillows, bumpers, doonas or cot toys
Baby sleeps on the back, in your room, for the first 6 to 12 months
Clear hanging cords and blind chains away from the cot
weeks.heads_up: Swaddling has rules too, and the hips are the bit people get wrong. Week minus 3.

weeks.title: Feeding kit and the freezer
weeks.headline: Future you, standing in the kitchen at midnight, is the person you are shopping for.

expect.feeds: Breast, bottle or both. All three are a real plan
expect.sleep: Expect to sleep in 2 to 4 hour blocks for a while
expect.newThisWeek: Baby is putting on roughly 200g a week from here

focuses: Batch cook 8 to 10 one-handed dinners and freeze them in portions
Set up a feeding spot: water, snacks, charger, lamp, muslins
If bottles are part of the plan, learn sterilising before you need it
weeks.heads_up: An antenatal breastfeeding session now beats learning it cold on day two.

weeks.title: Pack the bag and learn to swaddle
weeks.headline: Learning a swaddle today takes ten minutes. Learning it on no sleep takes a week.

expect.feeds: Colostrum first, drops at a time, and that is plenty
expect.sleep: Nap when you can. The sleep debt starts soon
expect.nappies: The first nappies are black and sticky. That is meconium
expect.newThisWeek: Baby is laying down fat and getting ready to breathe air

focuses: Pack the hospital bag, and a separate going-home bag for the car
Practise swaddling on a teddy: firm at the chest, loose at the hips
Put your numbers on the fridge: MCH nurse, GP, 13 HEALTH, 000
weeks.heads_up: Swaddling stops at the first sign of rolling, usually around 4 to 6 months.

weeks.title: Who does what, and when
weeks.headline: The night plan you agree while you are calm is the one that holds up at 3am.

expect.feeds: Plan around 8 to 12 feeds a day, around the clock
expect.sleep: Agree shifts now: one of you on, one of you asleep
expect.nappies: Expect 8 to 12 nappy changes a day, so stock two sizes
expect.newThisWeek: Baby is settling head down and gaining fat for warmth

focuses: Agree the night split out loud, including who does the 3am feed
Line up two people you would actually let hold the baby, and ask them
Fit the car seat and do a dry run of the drive home
weeks.heads_up: A midwife or MCH nurse visits you at home in the first 1 to 5 days. Keep that week clear.

weeks.title: Any day now
weeks.headline: Nothing left on the list beats rest. You are as ready as anyone actually gets.

expect.feeds: First feed often happens in the hour after birth
expect.sleep: Sleep now, in daylight, with your phone face down
expect.nappies: One wet nappy on day one is normal, then more each day
expect.newThisWeek: Full term is anywhere from 37 to 42 weeks, so this is normal

focuses: Charge everything, fuel the car, keep the bag by the door
Know your signs to ring the hospital, and who drives
Freeze one more dinner, then stop organising and rest
weeks.heads_up: Week one is feeding, nappies and almost no routine. That is the whole job.

weeks.title: The first week
weeks.headline: Nobody has a routine this week. Feed, change, hold, repeat, and let people help.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds in 24 hours, day and night, no pattern
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours total, in stretches of 2 to 4 hours
expect.tummyTime: 1 to 2 minutes, once or twice a day. Chest to chest counts
expect.nappies: Day 1: one wet nappy. By day 5: five or more heavy wets
expect.newThisWeek: Nappies go black, then green, then yellow once milk is in

focuses: Feed on their cues, not the clock, at least 8 times in 24 hours
Back to sleep, in your room, firm flat mattress, every single sleep
Say yes to the midwife or MCH home visit in the first 1 to 5 days
Keep the cord stump dry and the nappy folded below it
weeks.heads_up: Losing up to 10% of birth weight is normal, and it is usually back by 2 weeks.

weeks.title: Feeding finds its feet
weeks.headline: This week is mostly feeding. If the nappies are right, the feeding is working.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds, often every 2 to 3 hours
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, longest stretch 2 to 4 hours
expect.tummyTime: 1 to 3 minutes, two or three times a day
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wet nappies and 3 or more soft poos
expect.newThisWeek: Birth weight is usually back by the end of next week

focuses: Count heavy wet nappies, not millilitres, to see feeding is on track
Get attachment checked by the midwife or an ABA counsellor
Burp after every feed, upright against your shoulder
Sleep when they sleep, even at 11am, even badly
weeks.heads_up: A growth spurt lands around week 3. Feeding goes up, nothing has gone wrong.

weeks.title: The two week check
weeks.headline: You are two weeks in, which is longer than it feels. Small things first.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds, with an evening cluster most nights
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, still waking every 2 to 4 hours
expect.tummyTime: 2 to 3 minutes, around three times a day
expect.nappies: 5 or 6 heavy wets, and a poo after most feeds
expect.newThisWeek: The cord stump has usually dropped off by now

focuses: Weigh-in and a catch-up with the MCH nurse around now
A bath is optional. Top and tail two or three times a week
Add vitamin D or any supplement only if your nurse or GP says to
Get outside for 15 minutes with the pram, both of you
weeks.heads_up: Cluster feeding and a fussier baby around week 3. Stock the freezer.

weeks.title: Growth spurt and cluster feeding
weeks.headline: Feeding on and off all evening is a growth spurt, not a sign your supply is failing.

expect.feeds: More than last week, sometimes hourly for a run
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, and more restless in the evening
expect.tummyTime: 3 minutes, three times a day
expect.nappies: Still 5 or more heavy wets a day, poos vary
expect.newThisWeek: Crying is picking up, often worst in the late afternoon

focuses: Feed as often as they ask. Cluster feeding is how supply builds
Set up before the evening run starts: drink, snack, something to watch
Swap jobs. The parent not feeding does nappies and settling
weeks.heads_up: Crying peaks around 6 to 8 weeks, then eases. It is a phase, not a flaw.

weeks.title: One month in
weeks.headline: A month old. Nothing is sorted, and yet here you both are, doing it.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds, starting to find a loose shape
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, some babies give one 4 to 5 hour stretch
expect.tummyTime: 3 to 5 minutes, three times a day
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets, poos may space out a little
expect.newThisWeek: Focusing on your face at about 20 to 30cm away

focuses: Book the 6 to 8 week immunisations and the GP check now
Pick one settling routine and give it a week before you judge it
Swaddle for sleep if it helps: arms in, hips free, face clear
weeks.heads_up: Smiles turn up around 6 weeks, and they are worth the wait.

weeks.title: Louder, and nearly smiling
weeks.headline: The crying is climbing. That is normal, it peaks soon, and then it goes.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds, evening clusters are common
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, longest stretch 3 to 5 hours
expect.tummyTime: 3 to 5 minutes, three or four times a day
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poos every day or two
expect.newThisWeek: Cooing, gurgling, and the first almost-smiles

focuses: Hold, rock, walk. You cannot spoil a newborn by comforting them
Hand the baby over when you are past it. That is a plan, not failing
Check in on each other: how are you both actually sleeping
weeks.heads_up: The 6 to 8 week immunisations are due next week or not long after.

weeks.title: Smiles, needles and a growth spurt
weeks.headline: The hardest week often holds the first real smile. Both of those are true at once.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds, with a cluster-feeding run most evenings
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours total, longest stretch 4 to 5 hours
expect.tummyTime: 5 minutes, three or four times a day
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets, poos may drop to one a day
expect.newThisWeek: First proper smiles, aimed right at you

focuses: Get the 6 to 8 week immunisations done, with the GP check alongside
Expect an unsettled day after needles. Extra feeds and cuddles help
Ride out the growth spurt by feeding more often, not less
Book your own 6 week check, both of you if you can
weeks.heads_up: Crying peaks over the next fortnight, then eases off. You are near the top.

weeks.title: Peak crying
weeks.headline: If today felt like the worst yet, that fits. This is the top of the hill.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds, still clustered in the evening
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, longest stretch 4 to 6 hours
expect.tummyTime: 5 to 8 minutes, three times a day
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Up to 2 or 3 hours of crying a day is still normal

focuses: If you are rattled, put baby down somewhere safe and breathe for 5 minutes
Ring the MCH nurse or GP if the crying sounds different or they seem unwell
Put PANDA 1300 726 306 in both your phones, for either of you
weeks.heads_up: Most babies settle noticeably between 9 and 12 weeks. It really does ease.

weeks.title: Two months, and a shape appears
weeks.headline: The days start to have a shape. Not a schedule, but something you can see.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 breastfeeds, or 5 to 7 bottles, in 24 hours
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, 3 to 5 naps plus a longer night block
expect.tummyTime: 8 to 10 minutes a day, split into short bursts
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets, poos every 1 to 3 days
expect.newThisWeek: Holding their head up for a few seconds on their tummy

focuses: If the immunisations have not happened yet, book them this week
Start a simple wind-down: dim light, feed, sleeping bag, cot
Every sleep on the back, in your room, nothing loose in the cot
weeks.heads_up: Around 12 weeks a lot of babies stretch their night sleep noticeably.

weeks.title: The fog starts lifting
weeks.headline: More awake time, more smiling, a little less mystery. Things are changing.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds, evening clusters easing off
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, longest stretch 4 to 6 hours
expect.tummyTime: 10 minutes a day, across two or three goes
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Crying starts easing off from about now

focuses: Build tummy time to 10 minutes a day, while they are happy and awake
Talk and sing through nappy changes. This is their language lesson
Get one proper block of sleep each, on different nights if you must
weeks.heads_up: A GP or nurse check sits around 3 months. Write your questions down now.

weeks.title: Awake, alert and watching you
weeks.headline: They are properly interested in you now, and it makes the days easier.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds, bigger and a bit further apart
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, longest stretch 5 to 6 hours for some
expect.tummyTime: 10 to 15 minutes a day, in short bursts
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets, poos every 1 to 3 days
expect.newThisWeek: Following you across the room with their eyes

focuses: Check the car seat harness height. They outgrow a setting fast
Put them down awake once a day and see what happens
Get out daily: pram, park, coffee, anything with daylight in it
weeks.heads_up: Rolling can start from around 4 months, and swaddling stops when it does.

weeks.title: Hands, noise and splashing
weeks.headline: Hands have been discovered. Nothing is safe, and all of it goes in the mouth.

expect.feeds: 8 to 12 feeds, some babies drop a night feed
expect.sleep: 14 to 17 hours, often one 5 to 6 hour night stretch
expect.tummyTime: 15 minutes a day, broken into bursts
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poos settling into a pattern
expect.newThisWeek: Finding their hands, and chewing on them constantly

focuses: Make bath time part of the wind-down if they enjoy it
Lay them on a mat with one or two things to reach for
Dress for the room, not the forecast: about one layer more than you
weeks.heads_up: Dribbling and chewing is not always teeth. Teeth usually start around 6 months.

weeks.title: Three months: longer nights
weeks.headline: Plenty of babies stretch their night sleep around now. Plenty do not yet. Both are fine.

expect.feeds: 6 to 10 feeds, bigger and further apart
expect.sleep: 14 to 16 hours, longest stretch 5 to 7 hours for some
expect.tummyTime: 15 to 20 minutes a day, in short bursts
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Pushing up on forearms and holding their head steady

focuses: Expect a growth spurt: more feeds for a few days, then back to normal
Move the wind-down earlier if the evenings are falling apart
Watch for rolling signs, and stop swaddling at the first one
Book the 4 month immunisations and check now
weeks.heads_up: The 4 month sleep change is coming: more waking for a few weeks, then better.

weeks.title: A rhythm you can plan around
weeks.headline: You can roughly guess how the day will go now. That is the first real win.

expect.feeds: 6 to 10 feeds in 24 hours
expect.sleep: 14 to 16 hours, 3 or 4 naps and a longer night
expect.tummyTime: 20 minutes a day, in short happy bursts
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Laughing out loud, and grabbing at what they want

focuses: Keep the 4 month immunisations in the diary
Clear the floor space. Rolling is coming, and it arrives suddenly
Take one photo of them, and one of all three of you
weeks.heads_up: Around 4 months sleep often gets worse before it gets better. That is normal.

weeks.title: Four months: rolling and waking
weeks.headline: Sleep going backwards at 4 months is a development leap, not a mistake you made.

expect.feeds: 5 to 8 feeds or bottles in 24 hours
expect.sleep: 12 to 16 hours, 3 naps, night waking often increases
expect.tummyTime: 20 to 30 minutes a day, mostly rolling practice now
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Rolling, or very close to it. Hands to mouth with purpose

focuses: Stop swaddling now. Move to a safe sleeping bag with no hood
Never leave them on a change table or bed, not for a second
Get the 4 month immunisations done if you have not already
Ride the sleep change out: same wind-down, no new tricks for 2 weeks
weeks.heads_up: Solids start around 6 months, once they can sit supported and grab at food.

weeks.title: Nearly ready for food
weeks.headline: Watch for the signs, not the calendar. Food is weeks away yet, not days.

expect.feeds: 5 to 8 milk feeds a day, still the main event
expect.sleep: 12 to 16 hours, usually 2 or 3 naps
expect.tummyTime: Floor play most of the day, 30 minutes plus in bursts
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Sitting with support, and reaching for your plate

focuses: Watch for the solids signs: head steady, sits supported, grabs food
Buy a high chair with a harness and set it up early
Offer water from a cup when you start food. No juice
weeks.heads_up: First foods are iron-rich ones: iron-fortified cereal, meat, legumes, tofu.

weeks.title: Six months: first tastes
weeks.headline: Food starts now, milk still does the heavy lifting. Mess is part of the method.

expect.feeds: 5 to 7 milk feeds plus 1 or 2 small solid meals
expect.sleep: 12 to 16 hours, 2 or 3 naps, longer blocks overnight
expect.tummyTime: Sitting and rolling. Floor play whenever they are awake
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets. Poo changes colour and smell
expect.newThisWeek: Sitting on their own, and mouthing everything in reach

focuses: Start with iron-rich foods once or twice a day, after a milk feed
Offer one new food at a time and watch how they go with it
Get the 6 month immunisations done
Move the cot mattress to its lowest setting. They can push up now
weeks.heads_up: Teeth often arrive now. Most babies cope with chewing and a cold teether.

weeks.title: Two meals and sitting solid
weeks.headline: Food is becoming a routine. Sit together at the table and let them copy you.

expect.feeds: 4 to 6 milk feeds plus 2 small meals a day
expect.sleep: 12 to 15 hours, usually 2 or 3 naps
expect.tummyTime: Rolling, sitting, pivoting. Floor time all day
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Passing things hand to hand, and babbling in strings

focuses: Build up to 2 meals a day across a range of textures and tastes
Offer soft finger foods they can hold, like steamed vegetables
Baby-proof low down: power points, cords, stairs, cleaning cupboard
weeks.heads_up: Crawling and pulling up turn the house into a different place. Look down a lot.

weeks.title: On the move
weeks.headline: Crawling, shuffling or commando rolling. However they do it, they are off.

expect.feeds: 4 or 5 milk feeds plus 2 or 3 meals a day
expect.sleep: 12 to 15 hours, usually 2 naps
expect.tummyTime: They pick their own floor time now, and plenty of it
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets, poos firmer now solids are in
expect.newThisWeek: Crawling or shuffling, and the pincer grip starting

focuses: Finish the baby-proofing: gates, latches, cords, hot drinks up high
Three meals a day is the aim by around 9 months
Keep the cot empty: no bumpers, pillows, toys or loose bedding
weeks.heads_up: Separation anxiety often shows up from 8 months. Short goodbyes help.

weeks.title: Standing up and missing you
weeks.headline: Clinginess now is a sign of how attached they are, not a step backwards.

expect.feeds: 4 or 5 milk feeds plus 3 meals and a snack
expect.sleep: 12 to 15 hours, 2 naps, night waking can come back
expect.tummyTime: Pulling up on furniture, and cruising along it
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Pulling to stand, waving, and copying your sounds

focuses: Lower the cot base to its lowest setting before they stand up in it
Keep goodbyes short, cheerful and the same every time
Recheck the car seat. They may be ready for the next stage
weeks.heads_up: First steps land anywhere from 9 to 18 months. There is no late here.

weeks.title: Cruising the furniture
weeks.headline: Everything is a handrail now. Expect bumps, and expect them to be fine.

expect.feeds: 3 or 4 milk feeds plus 3 meals and snacks
expect.sleep: 12 to 15 hours, 2 naps, 11 to 12 hours overnight
expect.tummyTime: Standing, cruising, and climbing anything that holds still
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Pointing at what they want, and starting to understand no

focuses: Offer water in an open or free-flow cup with meals
Family food, cut small, with no added salt or sugar
Read the same book every night. The repetition is the point
weeks.heads_up: Cow's milk as a main drink waits until 12 months. In their food it is fine now.

weeks.title: Words and big opinions
weeks.headline: A first word may turn up this month, and so will the first proper protest.

expect.feeds: 3 or 4 milk feeds plus 3 meals and 2 snacks
expect.sleep: 12 to 15 hours, moving toward 1 or 2 naps
expect.tummyTime: Walking with help, and climbing the lounge
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Maybe a first word, and a lot of pointing and showing

focuses: Name whatever they point at. That is how words arrive
Let them feed themselves with a spoon, mess and all
Book the 12 month immunisations and check for around their birthday
weeks.heads_up: Fussy eating is common from about 1 year. Keep offering, and do not push.

weeks.title: Almost one
weeks.headline: They understand far more than they can say yet, which explains quite a lot.

expect.feeds: 3 milk feeds plus 3 meals and 2 snacks
expect.sleep: 12 to 15 hours, 1 or 2 naps
expect.tummyTime: Standing alone for a moment, and maybe a step
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Standing unaided, and following simple requests

focuses: Keep the 12 month immunisations in the diary
Plan the party small. One year olds do not need a crowd
The cot stays, with a sleeping bag, until they can climb out
weeks.heads_up: From 12 months, full cream cow's milk can become their main drink.

weeks.title: One year old
weeks.headline: A year ago none of you had done this before. Look at the three of you now.

expect.feeds: 3 meals, 2 snacks, and milk alongside, not instead
expect.sleep: 11 to 14 hours, 1 or 2 naps
expect.tummyTime: Walking or nearly, and into absolutely everything
expect.nappies: 5 or more heavy wets a day, poo daily to every few days
expect.newThisWeek: Walking, or getting there. Anywhere from 9 to 18 months

focuses: Get the 12 month immunisations and the health check done
Switch to full cream cow's milk as the main drink when you are ready
Check the car seat stage and the cot height one more time
Write down three things from this year before you forget them
weeks.heads_up: The 18 month immunisations are next. Toddler rules from here on.
